2. Listen and fill in the gaps.

 

 

I wanna talk about my experience of moving out and living on my own. Moving out to live on your own is not very (1)  in Hong Kong. Many people still choose to live with their parents even though they have a decent job and they’re already at their thirties. Many of them would stay with their parents until they (2) . There are several reasons behind – firstly, Hong Kong’s rent is expensive, many people would rather (3)  more money to purchase an apartment instead of renting one. Secondly, the Chinese traditional value of family is that the parents are the ones who (4) . When you become an adult, you should also (5)  your parents and you should (6)  more time to be with them. And of course there are people who are still dependent on their parents for food, clothing, (7) , etc.

When I tell people about the idea of moving out, many people’s reaction is like, “what do your parents say?” because they assume the parents would not like their children to leave them. Well I don’t know if my parents like it but I can tell you my parents (8)  my decision. They think it is good for me to try and live on my own and then I would know it is the best to stay with my family. The most important reason for (9)  is to save the travelling time to work. It used to take me (10)  to travel to work from my previous living place. From my new apartment, it just takes me (11)  minutes so I saved forty-five minutes’ traveling time. I don’t have to get up so early and I save two-third of my traveling cost. It does not only (12)  to travel for work but also from most of the places in Hong Kong.

In addition, I gain my personal space and (13)  by independent living. I make my own decision all the time, I do not have to say whether I would go home for dinner, I can (14)  my friends to come up and (15) .

Of course there are some trade-offs in living on your own. If you want to (16)  an apartment, there are lots of preparatory work to do. You have to keep visiting the apartments to search for your ideal one. You have to negotiate with the (17)  about the price, furniture inclusion, who is responsible for the (18)  of the furniture and equipment. My experience was that after we moved into the apartment, it was not until the kitchen cupboard was (19)  with water that we found out there was water leakage in the kitchen sink.

Money is the main issue in living on your own. You have to be (20)  all the expenses, for example, the rent, electricity, gas, water, telephone, internet bills, etc. Therefore you’ve got to be well prepared and save up for your bills.

Although I find my transportation time much shorter, the saved time is spent on other things, such as (21)  and some other household chores. I think preparing and cooking the food do occupy a significant portion of my time, therefore I always try to make simple meals. On the other hand, I have to regularly (22)  my apartment and wash my clothes, so it doesn’t really save much of my time after all.

Now everything is (23) , I’m getting used to my new life and I am enjoying it. I feel that moving out makes it easier for me to (24)  between my work, my (25) , my study and my family. It may be (26)  but it may worth.

Вопрос Инфо

Информационный текст

4. Discussion. Answer the questions.

1. How do you understand "on my own"? Explain with similar words and expressions. Have you heard this before?

2. Do you prefer living on your own or with your parents? Why? 

3. What are positive and negative things of living on your own?

4. Is money a crucial factor for you to decide whether to move out or not?

5. Speak about students' daily chores. How often and how easily do you deal with them?

6. Why in some cultures do young people tend to live with their parents before they get married? Take one country as an example, describe the situation and give your reasons briefly.
